prompt:
Read only the supplied evidence-document block or blocks and the complete fixed inventory of case assertions.

For every case assertion, find every explicit assertion in the supplied evidence text that materially bears on it. A bearing assertion must provide evidence for it, provide evidence against it, or materially qualify its scope, certainty, mechanism, population, timing, comparison, or conditions. Merely discussing the same topic is not bearing.

Return exactly one target envelope for every supplied propositionId, including targets for which this document block contains no bearing assertion. Do not add, delete, merge, split, rewrite, broaden, or narrow any case assertion. Do not decide whether a case assertion is true. Do not use outside knowledge. Query intent is not provided and must never be inferred as evidence stance.

For every bearing assertion return evidenceAssertion, bearingRelation (supports | challenges | qualifies | mixed), exactExcerpt, sourceLocation, whyItBears, confidence, quality, and limitationsVisibleInText. exactExcerpt must be copied literally from the supplied evidence text. confidence is certainty that the selected relation correctly describes this evidence-assertion/case-assertion pair; it is not truth probability. quality is pair-specific usefulness for evaluating that case assertion; it is not source quality, publisher quality, a final score, or a verdict.

The same evidence assertion may bear on more than one case assertion, but its relationship must be classified independently for each target. If no explicit assertion bears on a target in the supplied evidence text, return noBearingAssertionsFound true and an empty assertions array. For substantial_excerpt or abstract access, state text-visible access limitations without inferring absent full-text findings. Keep bearing relation, pair confidence, pair usefulness, source quality, access quality, and truth distinct.
